newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 23.

text.p: NZ Post's monopoly to end: Courier and freight companies could be delivering mail by next April, Communications Minister Maurice Williamson said on Tuesday when he announced the deregulation of postal services. Page 1.
Graham backs liquor sales deregulation: Justice Minister Doug Graham has come out in favour of complete deregulation of liquor sales, citing the example of the liberal Japanese system. Page 1.

Bolger denies Peters jumping gun on super: Prime Minister Jim Bolger tried on Tuesday to quell any impression that Treasurer Winston Peters was jumping the gun when he announced details of the proposed compulsory superannuation scheme last week. Page 1.

$1.1b needed to avert health crisis says Alliance: The public health system was on the brink of disaster, needing $1.1 billion to be spent urgently or hospitals will close, the Alliance said on Tuesday. Page 2.
PM defends plan for $94m building: Prime Minister Jim Bolger defended on Tuesday plans to build a $94 million ministerial building. Page 2.

Luxton urged to get fair share for all Maoris: Fisheries Minister John Luxton was pressed in Parliament on Tuesday to ensure Maori fisheries assets were allocated to both urban and rural Maoris. Page 2.

Labour queries arrest inaction: The government was reinforcing the suggestion that there was more than just confusion involved in the problems of the Dairy Board in Britain by its refusal to speak out in support of the board, Labour agriculture spokesman Jim Sutton and former trade minister Mike Moore said on Tuesday. Page 2.
Aussie beer 'could flood market': Australian brewers may flood the market with cheap beer if beer sales are allowed in supermarkets, sharemarket analysts says. Page 13.

Post competition tipped to benefit businesses: Businesses were likely to benefit more than individuals from the deregulation of NZ Post's domestic letter delivery service announced on Tuesday, industry players said. Page 13.
AMP has positive view on shares: The outlook for the New Zealand sharemarket was favourable for the next 12 to 18 months, giant fund manager AMP Investments said on Tuesday. Page 13.
Savings hit highest level in three years: Savers put $285 million into managed funds in the March quarter, the highest level in three years, according to IPAC Securities. Page 15.
Tip Top sale completed: HJ Heinz said it completed the sale of Tip Top, New Zealand's largest icecream maker, to closely held Peters and Brownes of Perth, Australia, for an undisclosed sum. Page 15.

Defiance drops 'don't sell' notice: Defiance Food Industries directors have dropped their "don't sell" recommendation to preference shareholders in favour of "no recommendation" after last week's increased offer for the company from South American-based Bunge Industries. Page 15.
Sales drop worries institute: The Real Estate Institute said on Tuesday that it was concerned by the sharp fall in rural property sales revealed in its latest survey. Page 15.

Macraes dispute requirement to backfill goldmine: The proposed expansion of the Macraes goldmine, near Palmerston in Otago, would not be viable if Macraes Mining Co was forced to fill in mined pits, company operations manager Philip Nolan said. Page 15.
